title_en: Wonders of Chinese Engineering (5/20): The China Sky Eye (FAST)
note_en: Spoken Chinese has one pronoun, tā, for "he," "she," and "it"; only the written characters differ: 他 for men, 她 for women, and 它 for things and animals. This text uses 它 for the telescope (它的反射面口径达到五百米 "its reflector is 500 meters across") and 它们 for the pulsars (它们的编号 "their designations"), since the plural just adds 们.

sentences.en: At this point Lucía closed her laptop and thought: Nan Rendong, the China Sky Eye's chief scientist and chief engineer, fought for this project for more than twenty years, yet he died in 2017 and never saw the many achievements the telescope would go on to make. Three years later, the Arecibo telescope she had known since childhood also collapsed when its steel cables snapped, leaving the China Sky Eye one of a kind. Sometimes, she couldn't help thinking, a scientist leaves this world and then the famous telescope back home falls too, and yet humanity has never stopped reaching for the stars.
